events.title: Telegram
events.text:
Defense Minister Israel Katz says he has instructed the military to impose a "general closure" on the West Bank, preventing Palestinian labourers from entering settlements.
 
Katz says that the IDF recommended the move, amid heightened tensions in the territory.
 
"As part of the directive, Palestinian workers will not be permitted to enter communities in Judea and Samaria during the Sukkot holiday," the defense minister says.
 
Still, Katz says that "essential workers" will be permitted to enter industrial zones in the West Bank, "in accordance with the security guidelines of the IDF Central Command."
 
Other exceptions may be given in accordance with "the state’s commitments to the High Court of Justice," Katz adds.
 
According to data from last year, some 9,000 Palestinians have permits to work in settlements or nearby industrial zones.

🇮🇷Iran says its military has evolved beyond conventional warfare
Iran’s Armed Forces have significantly expanded their capabilities since the 1980s Iran-Iraq War, with advances in missiles, drones, and asymmetric warfare, Brigadier General Abolfazl Shekarchi said, as cited by Tasnim News Agency.
🔊“Asymmetric warfare means standing up to the enemy’s expensive heavy weapons and achieving victory with lower costs and simpler, but more effective and practical, defense equipment,” Shekarchi said.
Shekarchi cited Iran’s missile program, which began during the war with Iraq, as an example of how external pressure accelerated the development of domestic defense technologies.
The Iranian general said the country’s missiles and drones have become more advanced and warned that any new aggression would be met with a response using “new military technologies.” He also said Iran maintains control over the security of the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for global energy shipments.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🪖🇮🇷 Iran has changed very nature of modern warfare, Pentagon’s former top future tech guy concedes
The US-Israeli 13k target assault on Iran in the first month of the war failed to break Tehran’s resistance, and left it “stronger than before” thanks to its ability to mount counterattacks and close Hormuz, says former US assistant secretary of defense for force development and emerging capabilities Michael C. Horowitz.
👉 The tools Iran used to do so – “a large arsenal of cheap yet accurate drones and missiles,” constitute a global paradigm shift, Horowitz wrote in a new Foreign Affairs piece.
The emergence of these weapons has made it impossible “for the US military, or any military, to win a full-blown war simply by using small numbers of exquisite weapons to dazzle opponents,” and enabled smaller countries to fight back using cheap, precision weapons to overwhelm pricy air and missile defenses.
💬 “The future of war lies in part in precise mass,” and “the world is learning from Iran” on this matter.
But it wasn’t by missiles and drones alone, Horowitz emphasized.
Iran has also spent years making “rigorous preparations” for defense by building a “vast underground network of missile infrastructure” which has proven impossible for the US and Israel to destroy, and “heavily dispersed missile production facilities” to go along with it.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🔥 Iran lays mines in the Strait of Hormuz targeting the Omani route — reports
Unconfirmed reports indicate at least some of the missiles fired into the Strait of Hormuz tonight carried naval mines — apparently dropped into the corridor through Omani waters that ships have been using to avoid Iranian clearance.
🔶 It is unclear how many mines were launched, or whether the deployment succeeded
🔶 The target appears to be the very route vessels have been using to evade the PGSA's transit requirements
🔶 Iran previously declared a restricted zone extending from the US Navy's blockade line through the strait and into the Persian Gulf
If confirmed, demining the Omani corridor would take time, ships, and sustained commitment from a US Navy that is already stretched to breaking. And every minesweeper sent into that corridor becomes a stationary target for Iranian forces.
Meanwhile, commercial vessels would have no choice but to obey the PGSA's designated safe route — because the alternative now has mines in it. That means Iranian clearance, Iranian paperwork, Iranian terms.
